summary: Adds an admin endpoint that deletes one user by id and an endpoint that purges a list of users.

findings.title: User delete route missing admin check
findings.problem: The DELETE /users/:id route does not run requireAdmin, unlike its sibling admin routes. Any caller who reaches the server can delete any user by id.
findings.consequence: A non-admin user can delete other user accounts. This causes data loss and breaks access control.
findings.fix: Add requireAdmin as middleware on the DELETE /users/:id route.

findings.title: Purge deletes run as unhandled floating promises
findings.problem: The forEach callback starts each async removeUser call, but nothing awaits or catches the returned promises. The handler sends the removed count before any delete finishes.
findings.consequence: removeUser throws for an unknown id, and the unhandled rejection crashes the Node process. The response reports every id as removed even when a delete fails.
findings.fix: Await Promise.all over ids.map with removeUser, or Promise.allSettled to count successes. Respond only after the deletes settle.
findings.suggested_change:
await Promise.all(ids.map((id) => db.removeUser(id)));
  res.json({ removed: ids.length });

findings.title: New delete endpoints have no covering test
findings.problem: The change adds two user delete endpoints, and the repository contains no test files. No test checks their authorization or error handling.
findings.consequence: Regressions in admin access checks or purge failure handling will ship unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add tests that a non-admin is rejected and that purge with an unknown id responds without crashing.
